articles.title: Here’s how CNN, Politico and MS NOW are responding to Trump’s White House ban
articles.summary: President Trump’s threat to ban three national news outlets from covering the White House is sparking rebuke from First Amendment advocates, elected Democrats and critics from across politics and media. In a Truth Social post Friday afternoon, Trump wrote he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House “effective immediately” for what…
articles.body:
President Trump’s threat to ban three national news outlets from covering the White House is sparking rebuke from First Amendment advocates, elected Democrats and critics from across politics and media.

In a Truth Social post Friday afternoon, Trump wrote he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House “effective immediately” for what he said was “a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!”

The president also suggested more outlets could be banned in the future and said no specific story or segment was sparking the ban, adding, “it’s really just cumulative stories over the last two years. You get sick of it.”

As of Friday evening, no reporters from any of the outlets mentioned in the president’s Truth Social post had reported being kicked off the White House grounds and the White House Correspondents’ Association had not weighed in on the president’s post.

Here’s what each outlet has said about Trump’s social media threat.

The Warner Bros. Discovery-owned network pushed back on the president for suggesting he would bar its journalists from covering his White House and said removing them from the grounds could violate the law.

“CNN stands fully behind our White House team and their fair and accurate reporting,” a spokesperson for the outlet said. “We have a right under the U.S. Constitution to do that reporting without hindrance or interference from the government.”

The cable news channel telegraphed potential legal action if Trump made good on his promise to keep its reporters from the White House.

“Should the ban which President Trump threatened go ahead, it would be an illegal assault on that fundamental and constitutionally-protected right,” the spokesperson said.

Trump has a long history of attacking CNN over its coverage of him and has specifically targeted anchor and reporter Kaitlan Collins in recent weeks over her questioning of him in the Oval Office.

Politico, an outlet that became the target of right-wing scorn during Elon Musk’s efforts to trim government spending, was also included in what Trump said was a soon-to-be-banned list.

Musk took issue with Politico Pro subscriptions during Department of Government Efficiency efforts he led, a service that many government employees and departments subscribe to for information and reporting on the inner workings of the federal government.

Trump, in his Truth Social post, suggested Politico was reporting “fake news” about him while benefiting from what he characterized as government subsidies.

“POLITICO will continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones,” the outlet said in a statement to The Hill on Friday. “We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them,” a spokesperson for the outlet said.

Of the accusations the outlet was taking money from the federal government, the outlet said, “the claims that POLITICO received government subsidies are false and have been thoroughly debunked.”

MS NOW declined to comment on the president’s threat, but its hosts and personalities have frequently been critical of Trump and his policies for years.

The progressive cable channel, formerly known as MSNBC, is home to the morning political talk program “Morning Joe,” which the president has attacked on numerous occasions during his years in office, and former Biden administration press secretary Jen Psaki.

articles.title: Trump touts Medicaid drug savings
articles.summary: All 50 states, Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico have applied to participate in an arrangement intended to give lower drug prices to Medicaid programs, President Trump said Friday. “This one thing alone should win us the midterms,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. Forty states and Puerto Rico have already signed agreements, the Centers…
articles.body:
All 50 states, Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico have applied to participate in an arrangement intended to give lower drug prices to Medicaid programs, President Trump said Friday.

“This one thing alone should win us the midterms,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.

Forty states and Puerto Rico have already signed agreements, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) said in a separate statement, and applying does not obligate states to participate.

The administration’s “generous” model allows participating states to purchase drugs at a price aligned with those in other countries. The theory, according to the CMS, is that it will allow state Medicaid programs to benefit from fairer, more competitive pricing.

The White House announcement comes as affordability is at the forefront of voters’ concerns ahead of the November midterm elections. To try to address those concerns, Trump has cut deals with pharmaceutical companies so the cost of some drugs in the U.S. would be tied to what companies charge other wealthy countries.

But critics say the administration is merely papering over the issue and has no real plan to deal with rising health costs — especially the ones caused when Republicans let ObamaCare’s enhanced premium subsidies expire.

The White House said participating pharmaceutical companies will provide state Medicaid programs with rebates on selected brand-name drugs to ensure the final price to Medicaid does not exceed what’s paid in other developed countries.

More than two dozen drug companies have agreed to participate in the program in exchange for tariff relief and exemptions from a similar pricing plan for Medicare.

“Medicaid programs will get the best possible price for drugs, delivering better value for taxpayers and freeing up funds to give vulnerable Americans the high-quality care they deserve,” CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz said.

The model includes hundreds of individual drugs across virtually all major drug classes, including oncology, diabetes care and asthma.

The White House Council of Economic Advisers estimated the “most-favored nation” (MFN) deals in Medicaid will produce $36.6 billion in federal savings and $27.6 billion for states.

But Medicaid drugs are already subject to steep discounts, and many of the details of the agreements are secret, so the true impact of MFN agreements on drug costs and accessibility isn’t clear.

Critics said there’s little evidence that drug companies are meaningfully lowering prices at all.

“Big Pharma expects little to no financial impact from these short-term Medicaid deals. Instead, pharma companies and Trump appear to have worked together to offer minor concessions to avoid taking more meaningful action to lower prices,” Peter Maybarduk, access to medicines director for Public Citizen, said in a statement, calling the agreements a “charade.”

articles.title: Republican highlights man freed from ICE custody in campaign ad
articles.summary: Rep. Monica De La Cruz (R-Texas) released a campaign advertisement featuring a man she helped get released Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody, along with his wife — who described the U.S.’s immigration system as “broken.” The ad, which first aired last week, shows an interview with a Weslaco, Texas, woman whose husband — a…
articles.body:
Rep. Monica De La Cruz (R-Texas) released a campaign advertisement featuring a man she helped get released Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody, along with his wife — who described the U.S.’s immigration system as “broken.”

The ad, which first aired last week , shows an interview with a Weslaco, Texas, woman whose husband — a Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) recipient — was detained by ICE.

The interviewee, named Stephanie, said he was freed after she reached out to De La Cruz — Texas’s 15th Congressional District incumbent locked in a tight race with Democratic challenger Bobby Pulido.

“My husband and I did things the right way, but we were stuck in a broken immigration system,” Stephanie said. “We need to secure our borders to keep our families safe, but this immigration system is broken. So, we reached out to Monica De La Cruz.”

“She helped with my husband’s immigration case. I’ve voted Democrat before, but Monica puts people over politics,” the woman continued.

De La Cruz is not the first Latina Republican to break with President Trump on immigration. On Thursday, Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar (R-Fla.) — running for reelection in Florida’s 27th Congressional District — released her own campaign video accusing the president of going “too far” with his escalated immigration enforcement operations.

“The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed today,” Salazar said.

Both Salazar and De La Cruz represent predominately Hispanic districts , according to census data.

Stephanie’s husband is not the first person the Texas Republican has gotten out of ICE custody. In March, she escorted Antonio Gámez-Cuéllar, a teenager detained for nearly two weeks, out of an immigration detention facility to his loved ones.

“This is about our community coming together for, not only their family, but other families who are in similar situations,” De La Cruz said at the time, adding that her colleagues in Congress should work on “common sense” enforcement policies, The Texas Tribune reported .

De La Cruz faces a fierce challenge from Pulido, who gained traction within the 15th District.

An August poll from Texas Southern University’s Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center reported that De La Cruz trailed Pulido by 5 points .

Cook Political Report’s July 16 update stated that “under normal circumstances, a district Trump carried by 18 points should not be competitive. But due to a number of unique factors” De La Cruz “faces a serious challenge from” Pulido.

De La Cruz has ramped up campaign efforts as November approaches, both through releasing this ad and giving a speech at Trump’s Republican National Committee midterm convention.

But De La Cruz still praised Trump for his handling of the U.S. southern border, saying in her ad , “Working with President Trump, we ended the border crisis, and today that border is safer than any point in history.”

articles.title: Trump announces agreement with Denmark to secure ‘permanent’ control over Greenland’s security
articles.summary: President Donald Trump announced a new deal with Denmark on Friday that grants the United States “permanent control over security” in Greenland.
articles.body: President Donald Trump announced a new deal with Denmark on Friday that grants the United States “permanent control over security” in Greenland. “I am pleased to announce that the United States of America has entered into an Agreement with The Kingdom of Denmark, and Greenland, that gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland, completely addressing ALL of our many U.S. concerns,” the president said in a post on Truth Social. Trump said the agreement comes at “NO COST” to the U.S. and that it is an “Infinite Life’ Agreement, there is no end!” The deal includes barring any U.S. adversary from ever being able to have a base or military presence in Greenland, or “make sensitive investments” there without written approval from the U.S., Trump said. A State Department official said in a statement to NBC News that the agreement explicitly bans any non-NATO base or troop presence in Greenland. It also includes screening mechanisms intended to block investments from Russia and China and bans them, and other adversaries, from making investments in Greenland that could threaten the U.S. “Greenland will forever be part of the strategic defense area of North America and exclude any adversary from it and the surrounding area,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement. “This deal permanently and completely addresses our national security concerns in Greenland.” Trump said that the administration will work with Greenland to immediately begin developing a “large Military presence in the appropriate part of Greenland, of which there are many.” “At my direction, we worked with representatives of Denmark and Greenland to guarantee that the United States will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the security of Greenland, and the United States of America,” Trump wrote. Leaders of Denmark and Greenland said in a statement Friday that Denmark, Greenland and the U.S. are expected to sign the agreement next week in connection with the upcoming United Nations General Assembly in New York City. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen emphasized in a statement Friday that the agreement does not give the U.S. sovereignty over Greenland. She described the deal as “an agreement that strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area and is therefore also good for NATO and Europe,” Frederiksen wrote. “And an agreement that at the same time recognizes the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination.” Jens-Frederik Nielsen, chairman of the Greenland government, wrote in a statement that the deal is “to the benefit of us all.” “It is gratifying that we are about to enter into an agreement that ensures and strengthens the security of Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, the United States and the Western alliance. The agreement recognizes Greenland’s interests and our place in international cooperation,” Nielsen wrote. A State Department official told NBC News that the agreement will remain fully in effect “forever,” including “if Greenland becomes a fully independent country” from Denmark. “The agreement explicitly guarantees the United States the complete ability to do what it deems is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the American continent, including permanent access, basing, and overflight rights,” the official said. “This agreement ensures the necessary U.S. military presence in Greenland permanently, allowing the U.S. military to increase the number of bases in Greenland as required.” The agreement to establish the American military presence in Greenland follows Trump’s threats in January to take the country “one way or the other.” While the president later toned down the threat of military action against Greenland, his administration continued its efforts to gain power there, including a visit from the U.S. special envoy to Greenland, Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry, in May. Trump’s approach to the country has sparked outrage from Greenlanders, who consistently have shown in polls that they overwhelmingly reject American annexation. Despite the strong opposition to Trump’s threats, Greenland’s government had been participating in negotiations alongside Denmark and the U.S. to find a solution on security concerns. Greenland has long been contested among the U.S., Russia and China because of its strategic position in the region and its vast mineral resources.

articles.title: Fox News contributors denounce Trump’s ban on CNN, MS NOW, Politico
articles.summary: Several contributors to Fox News offered stark criticism Friday of President Trump’s decision to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. Trump announced the decision in a Friday Truth Social post, saying the ban would be “effective immediately” for those outlets, “as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” He suggested…
articles.body:
Several contributors to Fox News offered stark criticism Friday of President Trump’s decision to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.

Trump announced the decision in a Friday Truth Social post , saying the ban would be “effective immediately” for those outlets, “as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” He suggested more outlets would be banned in the future.

Fox News contributor Ari Fleischer was quick to respond on social media Friday , writing, “I agree with POTUS that several media outlets covering the WH are biased and unfair.”

“Banning them from the WH is not the solution. Open the pool and the briefing room to conservatives. Challenge liberal reporters. Argue and defeat them,” he stated. “Don’t ban them. Or one day they’ll ban us.”

Fox News’s chief political analyst Brit Hume also wrote on social media that he “100%” agreed with a post from Jonathan Turley, a George Washington University Law School professor.

Turley called Trump’s move “terrible precedent and practice” that “would raise serious constitutional questions and undermine the country’s long-standing position as a voice for the free press.”

Hume added that if Trump “thinks this will lead to more favorable coverage, I think he’s dreaming.”

When asked in the Oval Office about the ban, Trump said he did it “because they’re fake news. You get so tired of reading and seeing fake news.”

“But our country has to have honest news,” he added.

The ban comes after Trump attempted to sue CNN for defamation for the outlet’s reporting on the 2020 election. He also sued The Wall Street Journal last year over its reporting on his alleged ties to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

articles.title: How do we still know so little about Thomas Crooks
articles.summary: One of the highest honors of my professional life was serving as director of communications for the late Sen. Bob Dole (R-Kan.). Because of his poor childhood; his heroic actions in World War II; the three years he spent in a hospital fighting to survive his almost mortal wounds; and the innate goodness within him,…
articles.body:
One of the highest honors of my professional life was serving as director of communications for the late Sen. Bob Dole (R-Kan.). Because of his poor childhood; his heroic actions in World War II; the three years he spent in a hospital fighting to survive his almost mortal wounds; and the innate goodness within him, I truly don’t know a human being who cared more for the suffering and disenfranchised of our nation, or who shed more real tears for them.

As the driving force behind Washington, D.C.’s World War Two Memorial, Dole not only morphed into “America’s veteran” but he also served as a political template for how to work across the aisle to get things done for the American people — most especially, its disabled citizens .

All of those positives and warm memories came flooding back into my mind after reading, of all things, news that the attempted Trump assassin, Thomas Crooks, used “Bob Dole” as an alias when ordering “suspicious packages.” Suddenly, Bob Dole’s name may be forever linked to a very troubled young man who killed one innocent bystander and wounded two others while attempting to assassinate Trump .

I first became a fan of Trump while working in the Reagan White House and after reading his bestselling book “The Art of the Deal.” I honestly believed it to be one of the best “real world” business books ever written.

Flash ahead to three days before the assassination attempt in Butler, Pa. Then a former president, Trump had been kind enough to invite me to his golf course in Jupiter, Fla., for a private breakfast and to hit the links. We spoke about golf, business and politics.

What most stuck with me about that very special moment was how incredibly kind and genuine Trump was to everyone at his country club. Not only did he know each staff member by name, he also knew the names of their children. He joked with them, laughed with them, and bonded with them. It showed a real side of him that the American people rarely get to see because of a highly adversarial mainstream media.

Like him or not, agree with him or not, this is a president who has been mercilessly attacked by journalists who have dubbed themselves part of what they call “the resistance.” He had the deep state of two previous administrations marshalled against him, and lawfare was used in an attempt to destroy his candidacy, imprison him or both. Far-left activist judges are still seeking to unwind or delay his policies and, in many cases, upend the will of the American people.

After engaging in one more conversation with Trump that day in 2024, I walked past his Secret Service detail and said, “Thank you for service and please protect him.” I felt the need to say that because I knew in three days’ time, the president would be attending yet another outdoor campaign rally, in Butler, Pa. Precisely because of the ever-escalating hateful rhetoric of the far left, I did fear it could trigger an already damaged mind.

Was that the case with Thomas Crooks? That is but one of an endless series of unanswered questions regarding that fateful day.

Douglas MacKinnon is a former White House and Pentagon official.

articles.title: Trump says US has reached an agreement to take permanent control of Greenland’s security
articles.summary: Greenlanders have voiced their opposition to U.S. control, holding anti-Trump protests with signs that read, ‘Make Americans Go Away’
articles.body:
President Donald Trump has announced an agreement with Greenland, granting the U.S. permanent control over the Arctic island’s security.

The agreement stipulates that U.S. adversaries such as Russia and China will require Trump's approval to engage with Greenland militarily and economically.

Despite opposition from Greenlanders, European allies, and a majority of Americans, Trump has declared the agreement as a significant achievement for national security.

President Donald Trump has announced an agreement with Greenland , in which the U.S. will take permanent control of the Arctic island's security.

"I am pleased to announce that the United States of America has entered into an Agreement with The Kingdom of Denmark, and Greenland, that gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland, completely addressing ALL of our many U.S. concerns," Trump wrote on Truth Social Friday evening.

The president has eyed Greenland since before he returned to the White House in January 2025, arguing that the U.S. needed to control the semi-autonomous Danish territory for national security purposes.

Trump said that the agreement means the U.S. "will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the security of Greenland, and the United States of America."

It's unclear what exactly is in the agreement Trump claims to have struck with Denmark and Greenland, but he did highlight one major point — U.S. adversaries such as Russia and China will need his approval to work with Greenland militarily and economically.

"From now on, no U.S. adversary can EVER have a base in Greenland, have a military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval," Trump said.

"It's so strategic. Right now, Greenland is covered with Russian and Chinese ships all over the place," Trump claimed during a press gaggle aboard Air Force One in January. "We need Greenland from the standpoint of national security — and Denmark is not going to be able to do it."

Trump boasted about his role in the new agreement with Greenland that he said would be "cherished by the American People."

"For over 100 years, Presidents have known the strategic importance of Greenland, but NONE of them were able to do anything about it. I am proud to be the President that permanently and conclusively addressed this very important situation," he wrote on Truth Social.

"We will immediately begin the process of developing a large Military presence in the appropriate part of Greenland, of which there are many. We will work with the people of Greenland in its development and construction," he added.

Since Trump began pushing to acquire Greenland, he has been met with opposition , not just from the people of the Arctic island and Denmark, but also from America's European allies.

"Greenland belongs to its people. It is for Denmark and Greenland, and them only, to decide on matters concerning Denmark and Greenland," a joint statement from seven European leaders read.

In the January 6 statement, leaders from France, Germany, the United Kingdom and other U.S. allies said, "We and many other Allies have increased our presence, activities and investments, tokeep the Arctic safe and to deter adversaries."

They said that since Denmark is a part of NATO, "security in the Arctic must therefore be achieved collectively...by upholding the principles of the UN Charter, including sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inviolability of borders."

Days later, Trump threatened to impose a 10 percent tariff on imports from European allies, several of which were part of the earlier joint statement, "until such time as a Deal is reached for the Complete and Total purchase of Greenland."

Trump quickly backed down from his tariff threats , claiming to have "formed the framework of a future deal with respect to Greenland" with NATO chief Mark Rutte .

Even with the new agreement between government officials, it is doubtful that Trump will sway those in Greenland opposed to American intervention.

The day Trump threatened tariffs against European nations if he did not strike a deal to acquire Greenland, protesters in Nuuk held Greenlandic flags and a banner that read "Make America Go Away" and "We Are Not Property!"

"I think he should mind his own business," Greenlander Lars Vintner, a heating engineer, told the Associated Press in January.

"What's he going to do with Greenland? He speaks of Russians and Chinese and everything in Greenlandic waters or in our country," he said. "Every summer we go sailing and we go hunting and I never saw Russian or Chinese ships here in Greenland."

A majority of Americans are also not sold on the idea of gaining control of Greenland.

Fifty-eight percent of Americans oppose a U.S. takeover of the Arctic island while 21 percent favor it and 20 percent are unsure, according to a Pew Research Center poll from January.

articles.title: Vance calls midterms a referendum on ‘common sense versus pure unadulterated crazy'
articles.summary: JD Vance rallied in Iowa, calling the midterms a referendum on common sense and targeting Democrats he says have abandoned the working man.
articles.body: Vice President JD Vance called out Democrats Friday, saying the midterms will be a referendum on "common sense versus pure unadulterated crazy." While stumping in Iowa, Vance said Democrats are no longer "the party my grandparents grew up talking about." Raised by a union steelworker, Vance said his father told him that "FDR’s Democrat party, that JFK’s Democrat party was the party of the workingman. THE ONE LINE FROM JD VANCE’S GOP KEYNOTE THAT REVEALS HIS VISION FOR AMERICA "This is not FDR’s party, as much as we might wish it was. It's not JFK’s party. Ladies and gentlemen, it’s not even Bill Clinton’s party." Vance said today’s Democrats don’t believe the country needs to be "built upon" but "utterly transformed." "In New York," he said, some of the midterm candidates are calling for the "total eradication of Western civilization. Somebody running for Congress in New York — and I promise I’m not joking about this — said that July Fourth is actually about the liberation of Palestine and Puerto Rico." To loud boos, Vance said, "You could almost laugh about" the idea of Thomas Jefferson writing the Declaration of Independence and thinking about the liberation of Palestine and Puerto Rico. MORNING GLORY: FIVE SENATE RACES SHOW WHY DEMOCRATS MAY REGRET THEIR PRIMARY CHOICES "But, unfortunately, it’s not funny because those people are dead serious, and this election is a referendum on common sense versus pure unadulterated crazy. Let’s send the crazy packing and get them out of Washington, D.C." Vance said to cheers. Vance also claimed some Democratic candidates are "out-and-out lunatics" who have "lost their ever-loving minds." "These are the ones who will tell you that our history is evil, and this country needs to be bulldozed and started over from the beginning," he continued. 'JESUS WAS A RADICAL': PROGRESSIVES INVOKE CHRIST TO SELL LEFT-WING AGENDA ON CAMPAIGN TRAIL But he said other Democrat candidates are "smart enough to realize that the country hasn't lost its mind, and, so, they try to be just a little bit more subtle." Calling out Democrat U.S. Senate candidate Adam Hamilton of Kansas, Vance claimed Hamilton gave off a "kind of ‘gee whiz, I’m a nice pastor’ vibe," but he's a man that tells his congregation not about the gospel of Jesus Christ, but that they need to repent for their White privilege." During the rally, Vance threw his support behind Iowa Republicans, including gubernatorial nominee Zach Lane, Rep. Ashley Hinson and congressional candidate Chris McGowan.

articles.title: Trump announces White House ban against three media outlets
articles.summary: President Donald Trump announced CNN, MS NOW and Politico are banned from the White House, dubbing them "fake news" and teased other outlets could follow.
articles.body: President Donald Trump announced Friday that CNN, MS NOW and Politico will be banned from the White House. "I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW ... and Politico ... from the White House as a result of their constant 'reporting' FAKE NEWS!" Trump wrote in a Truth Social post. Trump doubled down on his announced ban while taking questions from reporters at the Oval Office, citing "cumulative stories" the three outlets have published over the years. "You get sick of it," Trump said. CNN FIRES BACK AT TRUMP WHITE HOUSE OVER ATTACKS ON REPORTER, CALLS THEM 'BENEATH THE OFFICE' Trump denied he was trying to intimidate the press from doing its job in an exchange with another reporter. For decades, CNN has been part of a rotating pool of five networks, including Fox News, that travel with the president around the world. Notably, CNN has already been selected to lead network pool coverage Monday as Trump is set to attend the United Nations General Assembly. TRUMP BLASTS NEW YORK TIMES, CNN FOR 'SEDITIOUS' COVERAGE OF IRAN WAR Sarah Huckabee Sanders, the Republican Arkansas governor and former White House press secretary during the first Trump administration, was in attendance at the Oval Office event focused on healthcare and rejected the notion that Trump opposes a free press that's enshrined in the First Amendment of the Constitution. "I think it's hard for you to argue against a free press when you're literally standing in the Oval Office asking questions of the president of the United States," Sanders told reporters. "He has been more accessible and easier to talk to than any president in history." CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS Past efforts by the Trump administration to ban outlets and individual journalists have been blocked by federal judges. "I don't think that a court should allow fake news to be written day, after day, after day. I think that somebody has a right to keep them away," Trump said. Fox News senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy said CNN was still broadcasting live from its tent on media row outside the White House, but a senior White House official told him top brass at CNN, MS NOW and Politico were being informed that their journalists cannot be on White House grounds beginning Saturday. "CNN stands fully behind our White House team and their fair and accurate reporting," the network said in a statement on X. "We have a right under the U.S. Constitution to do that reporting without hindrance or interference from the government. Should the ban which President Trump threatened go ahead, it would be an illegal assault on that fundamental and constitutionally-protected right." Politico also issued a statement, telling Fox News Digital, "Politico will continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones. We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP A spokesperson for MS NOW declined to comment.

articles.title: Why the House let out early is a matter of debate after Johnson says chamber has 'done its work'
articles.summary: Thomas Massie claims Mike Johnson sent the House home early to dodge a vote on his eight privileged impeachment articles against Pete Hegseth.
articles.body: It’s a matter of debate as to why House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., sent the House home a day early this week. This is in addition to the House lopping off two additional weeks from its schedule later this month and into early October. "We're going to modify the House schedule by a day. And let me explain to you why. The House has done its work," Johnson said as House members fled Capitol Hill early Wednesday night. "House Republicans are going now back to our districts. We're going to make the case to the American people on what we have delivered on their behalf." The House isn’t scheduled to reconvene until Nov. 9, just after the midterms. But outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., believes there’s a different reason Johnson cut everyone loose early. The Kentucky Republican introduced eight articles of impeachment for Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth. Because Massie’s push for impeachment is "privileged," the House had 48 hours max to consider the articles. THE HITCHHIKER’S GUIDE TO MASSIE SAYING JOHNSON IS SENDING THE HOUSE HOME EARLY TO PREVENT HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT "I figured out why we canceled tomorrow," Massie said. "Tomorrow would be the vote on impeaching Secretary of Defense Peter Bryan Hegseth. And it looks like that vote's not going to happen." A senior House Republican leadership source insisted to Fox last week that members would be on Capitol Hill "for a full week." But, by Wednesday, the House had synced up with the Senate and passed the Russia sanctions bill. It OK'd legislation to protect consumers from high electricity and water bills associated with data centers, foisting the cost on tech companies. Yes, there were calls by bipartisan lawmakers that the House should remain in session to address intensifying concerns about AI. But the House was running out of floor traffic. Except for Massie’s measure to impeach Hegseth. REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: HOUSE CONTROL COULD HINGE ON WHETHER THE OLD POLITICAL RULES STILL APPLY Now you can determine for yourself why Johnson dismissed lawmakers a day early — to say nothing of the plan for the House to cut town two weeks sooner than originally planned. But you can imagine what Massie thought. "Exactly what I predicted," Massie said on the House floor. "Why did he just cut another day off the calendar?" I found Massie off the floor after he concluded his speech. "Do you think they adjourned the House because you have the votes on Hegseth?" yours truly asked. "Chad, they cut two weeks off of the calendar to keep me from getting to 218 votes on the Epstein discharge petition. And then we came into this week, and I introduced eight articles of impeachment against Peter Hegseth, and they have 48 hours to vote on that," Massie replied. "He cut off the day tomorrow to avoid the vote." Here are the parliamentary mechanics. The House was compelled to consider Massie’s impeachment articles if it met this past Thursday. Otherwise, the resolution covering the eight impeachment articles would expire. The 48-hour window associated with such privileged resolutions disappears. Sure. Massie could bring them up when the House next meets in November. But that is seven weeks from now. But let’s say the House met on Thursday and was forced to bring up Massie’s impeachment articles. Republicans would likely have offered "a motion to table." This is an effort to kill Massie’s gambit. Thus, the vote would not have been on impeaching Hegseth, but whether or not to set aside Massie’s plan. If the House voted to table Massie’s articles of impeachment, the gig is up. It’s done. The House never even considered the actual impeachment resolutions. The vote was one step removed from a straight, up/down vote on actually impeaching Hegseth. But let’s say the motion to table was to fail? That means the House immediately skips to the articles of impeachment. The possibility suddenly exists that Hegseth could face eight impeachment votes even through there’s been no investigation. No committee hearings. No "process." Nowhere does it say in the Constitution that Congress is required to wrestle with the usual parliamentary volutions to impeach someone. If a simple majority in the House votes to impeach you, you’re impeached. Nuff said. REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS MEETS AI AS FEARS OF HUMAN EXTINCTION JOLT CAPITOL HILL This is why Republicans likely would have moved to table Massie’s impeachment articles. A vote to table inoculates members from having to take a challenging vote on the underlying issue. Keep in mind that there are a number of House Republicans who are aggravated with Hegseth and beside themselves about the war in Iran. This vote would have put them in an interesting position, especially since many if not all Democrats may have voted to impeach. So, I asked Massie the following about the motion to table. "That would have put (members) in a tough spot. Or, if they had to vote on that, would it have passed?" I asked. "A vote on a motion to table? He may not have survived that vote," Massie declared. In other words, Massie believes the House could have defeated the motion to table. That would have triggered votes on actually impeaching Hegseth. And, from Massie’s standpoint, that’s why Johnson sent the House home. You might remember that there was a bipartisan effort last summer by Massie and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., to go around Johnson and deposit a measure on the floor, forcing release of the Epstein files. Johnson let the House out early for summer break then. Later, Johnson kept the House out of session for most of the 43-day government shutdown as the special effort to bring action on the resolution loomed. The House voted to reopen the government in mid-November. And one of the first things the House did after that? Voted 427-1 to require a release of the files. The lone nay vote against releasing the files? Rep. Clay Higgins, R-La. Even though there aren’t votes until early November, Massie is still a member of the House. He’ll be a member in the lame duck session through early January. Massie lost his primary to Republican Ed Gallrein, a candidate backed by President Donald Trump. And Hegseth took the unusual step of traveling to northern Kentucky this spring to campaign for Gallrein. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP It’s unclear if the Hegseth articles of impeachment will return late this fall or winter. But Massie is back. At least for a little while. And whether Johnson adjourned the House to prevent a vote on the impeachment articles will remain a matter of debate.
